newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Mol rally pushes Hungary BUX to new high.
newsitem.headline: Mol rally pushes Hungary BUX to new high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exhange rose to new record territory on Monday, propelled by the surging stocks of oil and gas company MOL, traders said.
The BUX index closed at the second successive new high of 5,496.56 points, up 58.21.
"The index went up but the only reason was MOL's rally," said Geza Raner of Bank Austria -GiroCredit Befektetesi Rt.

Shares in oil company MOL were the day's top performers. Of the day's total spot share turnover of 3.40 billion forints, MOL accounted for 1.67 billion and soared to a new record high of 3,300 forints before retreating to close at 3,200, up 120.
Traders attributed Monday's rise to market talks of good annual results. "The market expects very good results from MOL," one trader said earlier today.
Monday's surge in MOL's price follows an eight percent gain on Friday, propelled by a wage settlement.

The day's other gainer was canned food maker Globus, which soared more than 20 percent to a new record high of 2,150 percent, triggering a suspension of its trading for the day due to too rapid intraday rise.
Globus' rally came after news that the government has restored subsidies for its canned goulash exports.
Company CEO Miklos Olah told Reuters Globus expected the subsidy change would raise Globus's 1997 turnover by between 200 million and 400 million forints, and its profits by a couple of million.

A more thorough look on price movements showed that many other leading stocks of the Hungarian market reached their peak, at least temporarily, with investors ready to sell and hesitant to buy at current levels, traders said.
Elsewhere on the market, the pharmaceuticals and chemicals stocks moved lower.
Borsodchem ended at 5,990 forints, down 160, TVK at 2,545, down 30. Richter closed at 10,950 forints, down 200 and Egis at 11,500, down 135.
